texts.value: Catalyzes the formation of pyruvate in the last step of glycolysis, it is irreversible under physiological conditions. The reaction is critical for the control of metabolic flux in the second part of glycolysis
Belongs to type I PK; fructose 1,6-bisphosphate-activated
Carbohydrate degradation; glycolysis; pyruvate from D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate: step 5/5

Can be lactylated on Lys-382 (PubMed:36333310). Delactylated by the delactylase CobB (PubMed:36333310). Lactylation reduces activity of the enzyme and slows bacterial growth (PubMed:36333310). Lactylation may hinder the binding between fructose 1,6-bisphosphate (FBP) and PykF and weaken the allosteric activation of PykF, finally reducing the activity of PykF (PubMed:36333310). Delactylation by CobB regulates PykF activity and influences bacterial growth (PubMed:36333310)
Belongs to the pyruvate kinase family

texts.value: Catalyzes the phosphorylation of D-fructose 6-phosphate to fructose 1,6-bisphosphate by ATP, the first committing step of glycolysis (PubMed:2953977, PubMed:3158524). In addition, is involved in the utilization of D-sedoheptulose 7-phosphate, an intermediate of the pentose phosphate pathway, via the sedoheptulose bisphosphate bypass pathway (PubMed:19756045). Catalyzes the phosphorylation of D-sedoheptulose 7-phosphate to D-sedoheptulose 1,7-bisphosphate (PubMed:19756045)
Allosterically activated by ADP and other diphosphonucleosides, and allosterically inhibited by phosphoenolpyruvate
Carbohydrate degradation; glycolysis; D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate and glycerone phosphate from D-glucose: step 3/4
Reduces growth on glucose by 50% and causes a decrease in native reaction flux but increases the TCA cycle flux (PubMed:31390539). Secretes glucose into the medium (PubMed:31390539)
Belongs to the phosphofructokinase type A (PFKA) family. ATP-dependent PFK group I subfamily. Prokaryotic clade 'B1' sub-subfamily
